source_title: Thanksgiving Wine Choices to be Thankful For
newsletter_intro: Thanksgiving dinner can get busy fast, so I like to keep the wine list flexible and food-friendly. If your table leans Caribbean, Indian, African, Taiwanese, or just plain classic turkey, these picks can help you cover a lot of ground. Let’s make the holiday glass feel easy.

slides: Thanksgiving wine picks that can handle the whole table

Chardonnay with lift works beautifully with turkey and conversation
Cool-climate Pinot Noir and Gamay bring bright fruit and easy pairing
Cabernet Franc loves rice dishes, noodle dishes, and spice-forward plates

instagram_reel.hook: If your Thanksgiving table has turkey, spice, and dessert all at once, here’s the wine plan.
instagram_reel.script:
Thanksgiving is a lot. You’ve got turkey, sides, maybe some Caribbean or spice-forward dishes, and dessert too. So I like to keep the wines flexible.

A crisp Chardonnay works well with turkey. Cool-climate Pinot Noir and Gamay are great when you want lighter reds that can handle a mixed table. Cabernet Franc is a smart move if rice dishes, noodle dishes, or more savoury plates are showing up.

And for dessert? Make sure the wine is at least as sweet as the pie. That’s the easy rule.

If you want the full guide, I’ve put the pairings together in the post.

Thanksgiving can be a lot of different flavours on one table, so I like wines that can keep up.

A crisp Chardonnay is great with turkey. Cool-climate Pinot Noir and Gamay are easygoing reds for mixed plates. Cabernet Franc is a really nice choice if you’ve got rice dishes, noodle dishes, or anything with a little more spice.

And for dessert, remember this: the wine needs to be at least as sweet as the pie.

linkedin.post:
Thanksgiving menus are rarely simple. In many homes, the table includes turkey alongside spice-forward dishes, shared sides, and a dessert course that deserves its own pairing.

That is why I like to think in terms of versatility when building a holiday wine list.

A crisp Chardonnay can work beautifully with turkey. Cool-climate Pinot Noir and Gamay offer lighter red options that stay friendly across a mixed table. Cabernet Franc is especially useful when the meal includes rice dishes, noodle dishes, or more savoury, aromatic flavours.

For dessert, the simplest guideline is still one of the best: the wine should be at least as sweet and rich as the dish on the plate.

Holiday hosting gets easier when the wine is chosen with the whole menu in mind.
